name: Agriculture
blurb: Vision-guided spraying, yield prediction, and autonomous equipment at commercial scale, tracked through USDA ERS, FAO, satellite data providers, and the equipment and standards bodies.

points.desc: Deere's precision agriculture line (See and Spray, autonomous tractors) is the reference commercial deployment.
points.name: Precision ag is shipping product

points.desc: Census BTOS covers agriculture-adjacent sectors in its fortnightly AI-use series.
points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

points.desc: The Economic Research Service publishes the data series on precision-agriculture adoption across US farms - variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, autonomous equipment. The federal measurement layer.
points.name: USDA ERS measures US adoption

points.desc: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization's digital agriculture program, with the 60 Decibels-supported Digital Agriculture Index, benchmarks platform adoption and real-world yield and income impact.
points.name: FAO benchmarks digital agriculture globally

points.desc: The AgriFoodTech investment research tracks venture capital into agricultural AI, robotics, computer vision, and farm-management software - the sector's funding barometer.
points.name: AgFunder indexes the investment flow

points.desc: Planet Labs' high-resolution imagery, Descartes Labs' geospatial ML, and EarthDaily's field-level crop indicators supply the AI-ready observation data behind yield prediction and crop-stress detection.
points.name: The satellite layer feeds the models

points.desc: The Association of Equipment Manufacturers covers autonomous machinery, AI hardware standards, and robotics adoption across crop and livestock production.
points.name: AEM tracks the machinery standards

points.desc: The nonprofit consortium sets the open data standards that let AI models ingest feeds from tractors, drones, soil sensors, and satellites - the plumbing under everything else.
points.name: AgGateway makes the data interoperable

points.desc: The International Society of Precision Agriculture is the scientific organization connecting academic research on remote sensing and spatial analytics to commercial practice.
points.name: ISPA bridges the science and the field

points.desc: The 100 Million Farmers initiative tracks AI adoption through the lens of climate-smart and regenerative agriculture metrics globally.
points.name: WEF tracks climate-smart adoption

points.desc: Bayer's Climate FieldView and Corteva's Granular are the large digital-farming platforms turning soil, weather, and yield data into planting and input prescriptions with machine learning.
points.name: The agribusiness platforms run the prescriptions

points.desc: CNH Industrial's Raven division builds driverless tractor technology, AI path-planning, and precision application - the equipment layer beyond Deere.
points.name: CNH and Raven automate the other fleets

points.desc: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder kills weeds with computer vision and lasers instead of herbicide; Monarch builds electric driverless tractors - narrow AI shipping as farm equipment.
points.name: The pure-plays attack single problems

summary: Precision agriculture - vision-guided spraying, yield prediction, autonomous equipment - is deployed at commercial scale. Who tracks it: federal adoption data, a UN benchmarking framework, a venture index, and standards bodies, layered over the equipment giants and AI pure-plays actually shipping it.

analysis.body:
According to the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey, 13.7% of firms in agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting reported using AI in the prior two weeks, a figure that offers the clearest available measure of current penetration across the sector as a whole. The prior period estimate was suppressed, so directional change cannot be confirmed from that source alone, but the 13.7% reading places agriculture among the sectors where adoption is measurable and real rather than merely anticipated.

The clearest commercial deployments concentrate in two areas: field-level decision support and autonomous or semi-autonomous equipment. Climate FieldView, the digital farming platform, reports that farmers using its seed scripts saw an average increase of plus five bushels per acre compared to users who wrote their own scripts, a concrete yield figure attached to a machine-learning workflow. Carbon Robotics describes its LaserWeeder system as powered by a Large Plant Model trained on what it calls the world's largest and fastest-growing agricultural dataset, using computer vision to identify and destroy weeds with lasers in place of herbicide, and its Carbon Autonomy system extends the same physical AI approach to broader autonomous field operations. Planet Labs supplies the observation layer behind many of these systems, combining daily satellite imagery with analytics tools that allow crop monitoring, stress detection, and field-level change tracking at a cadence that earlier remote sensing could not match.

On the investment side, AgFunder reports that global agrifoodtech funding reached 16.2 billion dollars in 2025, nearly flat against the prior year at negative three percent, but with investors directing capital more selectively toward companies with what AgFunder describes as tangible science, real unit economics, and clear paths to revenue. The same research recorded 16 billion dollars in 2024, a four percent decline from 2023, though Asia-Pacific showed a 38% increase in funding through October 2024 relative to the same period in 2023, reaching 4.2 billion dollars. Developing markets overall saw funding grow 63% between 2023 and 2024 even as the global total slipped four percent, suggesting that geographic expansion of AI-enabled agriculture is continuing even as mature-market venture enthusiasm moderates.

The infrastructure enabling AI in agriculture depends on interoperability and data standards that most farmers never see directly. AgGateway, a nonprofit consortium, works to connect data flows from tractors, drones, soil sensors, and satellites through open standards, and its Traceability Initiative spans seeding, provenance, and grain traceability in North America while a parallel effort in Europe focuses on standardized farm and crop-field identification. The International Society of Precision Agriculture bridges academic research on remote sensing and spatial analytics to commercial practice, and the Association of Equipment Manufacturers brings together agricultural equipment original equipment manufacturers to shape policy and standards around autonomous machinery and AI hardware. FAO's digital agriculture program has engaged with AI adoption benchmarking in developing regions, including a partnership with Smart Africa on an Innovate Africa Challenge aimed at accelerating AI solutions for agricultural and climate challenges on the continent.

For an operator weighing deployment, the sourced evidence points to a sector where yield and cost benefits are documented for specific tools, investment is concentrating on ventures with demonstrable economics rather than early-stage promises, and the data plumbing required for AI to work reliably, including satellite feeds, standardized field identifiers, and interoperable equipment data, is still being built out rather than assumed. Adoption at 13.7% leaves most firms outside current use, which may reflect both the capital intensity of precision equipment and the data infrastructure gaps that organizations like AgGateway and ISPA are working to close. A prospective deployer should expect meaningful integration work and should evaluate vendor claims against the kind of field-level outcome data that platforms like FieldView are beginning to publish.
